# Instance chart {#sec-instance-charts} ::: {.callout-tip appearance='simple' icon=false} ***This graph is largely complete and just needs final proof reading.*** ::: :::: {.callout-note collapse="false" icon=false}
::: {.cell layout-align="right"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](instance_chart_files/figure-html/full_code_display-1.png){fig-align='right' width=60% height=60%} ::: ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #02577A;"} **Requirements:** ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.05em; color: #282b2d;"} **✅ a categorical variable** ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.05em; color: #282b2d;"} **✅ a numeric (count) variable** ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.05em; color: #282b2d;"} **✅ a numeric (date) variable** ::: :::: ## Description An instance chart (or instance graph) displays frequencies (or 'instances') of different categorical values over time. The time dimension is placed on the `x` and each separate categorical item is placed on the `y`-axis. The instances are typically represented using the vertical hashes from `geom_point()` (i.e., shape `124` or the 'pipe' `"|"`). Saturation and color are also used to represent different categorical levels and counts. ## Set up ::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; color: #1e83c8;"} **PACKAGES:** ::: Install packages. ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} library(ggplot2) library(dplyr) # for data manipulation library(tidyr) # for expand_grid() ``` ::: ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; color: #1e83c8;"} **DATA:** ::: *Rugrats* premiered on Nickelodeon in 1991, and a generation of parents suddenly had new ideas for baby names. We'll simulate how many babies were given each Rugrats character's name at one hospital every year from 1980 to 2005. Each name in `rugrats_names` has an average number of babies per year `before` the character's `debut` and an average `after` it (Susie showed up in 1992, Dil in 1998, and Kimi in 2001). `rpois()` draws each year's count (`n`) from the matching average. Setting the seed with `set.seed()` means you'll get the same 208 name years every time you run the code below. ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} rugrats_names <- tibble( name = c("Tommy", "Chuckie", "Angelica", "Phil", "Lil", "Susie", "Dil", "Kimi"), before = c(4, 0.3, 1, 1.5, 0.2, 1, 0.05, 0.05), after = c(8, 1.5, 4, 1.5, 0.8, 1.5, 2, 3), debut = c(1991, 1991, 1991, 1991, 1991, 1992, 1998, 2001)) set.seed(1993) hospital_names <- expand_grid(year = 1980:2005, rugrats_names) |> mutate(name = factor(name, levels = rugrats_names$name), avg_n = if_else(year < debut, before, after), n = rpois(n(), lambda = avg_n)) |> select(year, name, debut, avg_n, n) glimpse(hospital_names) #> Rows: 208 #> Columns: 5 #> $ year 1980, 1980, 1980, 1980, 1980, 1980… #> $ name Tommy, Chuckie, Angelica, Phil, Li… #> $ debut 1991, 1991, 1991, 1991, 1991, 1992… #> $ avg_n 4.00, 0.30, 1.00, 1.50, 0.20, 1.00… #> $ n 3, 0, 0, 2, 0, 1, 0, 0, 6, 0, 1, 3… ``` ::: ::: An instance chart only shows the years a name was used, so we'll filter out the years with no babies and store the rest in `rugrats_babies`. ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} rugrats_babies <- hospital_names |> filter(n > 0) glimpse(rugrats_babies) #> Rows: 128 #> Columns: 5 #> $ year 1980, 1980, 1980, 1981, 1981, 1981… #> $ name Tommy, Phil, Susie, Tommy, Angelic… #> $ debut 1991, 1991, 1992, 1991, 1991, 1991… #> $ avg_n 4.0, 1.5, 1.0, 4.0, 1.0, 1.5, 1.0,… #> $ n 3, 2, 1, 6, 1, 3, 3, 2, 1, 3, 1, 3… ``` ::: ::: ## Distribution An instance chart is built from two things: whether a name shows up in a given year (the tick), and how many times it shows up (the shading). The empty spaces between the ticks matter just as much as the ticks, and the number of empty spaces depends on how popular the name is. Below we'll move from the counts, to a picture, to the formula. ::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"} **COUNT IT:** ::: Start with Chuckie in the five years before and after the show premiered. ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} hospital_names |> filter(name == "Chuckie", year >= 1986, year <= 1995) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: ::: Before 1991, most years have no Chuckies at all. Below we count the years with zero babies (`zero_years`) for each name, before and after its character's debut. ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} zero_counts <- hospital_names |> mutate(era = if_else(year < debut, "before", "after")) |> group_by(name, era) |> summarise(years = n(), zero_years = sum(n == 0), .groups = "drop") |> pivot_wider(names_from = era, values_from = c(years, zero_years)) |> select(name, years_before, zero_years_before, years_after, zero_years_after) zero_counts ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: ::: Chuckie went 8 of 11 years without a baby before the show, and only 3 of 15 years after it. Tommy, the most popular name, never had a year without a baby. ::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"} **DRAW IT:** ::: The graph below draws Chuckie's yearly counts as bars (including the zeros) and the same years as instance ticks across the bottom. Every gap in the ticks is a year with a bar of height zero. ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} chuckie <- hospital_names |> filter(name == "Chuckie") ggplot(chuckie, aes(x = year)) + geom_col(aes(y = n), fill = "#F7941D") + geom_point(data = filter(chuckie, n > 0), aes(y = -0.5), shape = 124, size = 5, color = "#7B3FA0") + geom_vline(xintercept = 1990.5, linetype = "dashed") + labs(x = "Year", y = "Babies named Chuckie") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](instance_chart_files/figure-html/draw_inst-1.png){width=576} ::: ::: ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"} **NAME IT:** ::: Each yearly count follows a [Poisson distribution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poisson_distribution) with the average for that name and era: $$ n_{\text{name, year}} \sim \text{Poisson}(\lambda), \quad P(n = 0) = e^{-\lambda} $$ The chance of an empty year depends only on $\lambda$. Before the show, Chuckie's average is 0.3 babies a year, so $P(n = 0) = e^{-0.3} \approx 0.74$, and we'd expect about $11 \times 0.74 \approx 8.1$ empty years out of 11. After the show, the average jumps to 1.5, so $P(n = 0) = e^{-1.5} \approx 0.22$ and we'd expect about 3.3 empty years out of 15. Tommy averages 8 babies a year after the show, so an empty year has a chance of $e^{-8} \approx 0.0003$ (practically never). That's why rare names look like scattered ticks and popular names look like solid lines. Try changing Chuckie's `after` value to `5` and his row fills in. ## Grammar ::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; color: #1e83c8;"} **CODE:** ::: - Create labels with `labs()` - Initialize the graph with `ggplot()` and provide `data` - Map `year` to `x`, `name` to `y`, and `color` to `name` - Add `geom_point()`, map `n` to `alpha`, and set the `shape` to `124` and `size` to `5` - Most years have only a few babies, so we raise the lightest `alpha` with `scale_alpha_continuous(range = c(0.35, 1))` (otherwise the faint ticks disappear) - Remove the `color` legend with `guides()` (the names are already on the `y` axis) ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} labs_inst_rugrats <- labs( title = "Rugrats baby names", caption = "Simulated data", subtitle = "Babies named at one hospital, 1980 - 2005", x = "Year", y = "Name") ggp2_inst_rugrats <- ggplot(data = rugrats_babies, mapping = aes(x = year, y = name, color = name)) + geom_point(aes(alpha = n), shape = 124, size = 5) + scale_alpha_continuous(range = c(0.35, 1)) + guides(color = "none") ggp2_inst_rugrats + labs_inst_rugrats ``` ::: ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; color: #1e83c8;"} **GRAPH:** ::: ::: {.cell layout-nrow="1"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](instance_chart_files/figure-html/create_graph_inst-1.png){width=100% height=100%} ::: ::: ## More info ### Saturation with `cut_interval()` `ggplot2` has two great functions for splitting numerical variables into intervals or widths. We'll use `cut_interval()` to create an `n_range` variable, which splits the yearly counts (`n`) into intervals based on the `length` argument. ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} rugrats_babies_range <- rugrats_babies |> mutate(n_range = ggplot2::cut_interval(x = n, length = 3)) rugrats_babies_range |> count(n_range) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: ::: Below we can see the count ranges have been built with the [interval notation](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/cut_interval.html): `"(a,b]"` - Most of the ticks fall in the lowest range, and every count above 9 belongs to Tommy after the show premiered. ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} labs_inst_rugrats_range <- labs( title = "Rugrats baby names", caption = "Simulated data", subtitle = "Babies named at one hospital, 1980 - 2005", x = "Year", y = "Name", color = "Babies per year", alpha = "Babies per year") ggp2_inst_rugrats_range <- ggplot(data = rugrats_babies_range, mapping = aes(x = year, y = name, color = n_range)) + geom_point(aes(alpha = n), shape = 124, size = 4) + scale_alpha_continuous(range = c(0.35, 1)) ggp2_inst_rugrats_range + labs_inst_rugrats_range ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](instance_chart_files/figure-html/code_graph_inst_range-1.png){width=576} ::: ::: ::: ### Facets with `cut_number()` To demonstrate facets, we'll create two other variables: `year_range` and `group`: - `year_range` uses `ggplot2::cut_number()` to split the `year` into three groups with about the same number of ticks in each, then we build a label for each group from its first and last year - `group` is a factor variable with two levels: `"Babies"` and `"Big kids"` (Angelica and Susie) ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} rugrats_babies_fct <- rugrats_babies |> mutate(year_grp = ggplot2::cut_number(year, n = 3, labels = FALSE)) |> group_by(year_grp) |> mutate(year_range = paste(min(year), "-", max(year))) |> ungroup() |> mutate( year_range = factor(year_range, levels = unique(year_range[order(year)])), group = if_else(name %in% c("Angelica", "Susie"), "Big kids", "Babies"), group = factor(group, levels = c("Babies", "Big kids"))) ``` ::: ::: Below we can see the total counts of names in the cross-table of `year_range` and `group` ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} rugrats_babies_fct |> count(year_range, group) |> pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = n) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: ::: In the graph, we'll create labels using the `levels` from the `year_range` variable. - We can also change the `shape` used in `geom_point()` to the pipe operator (`"|"`) - With `scales = "free"`, each panel picks its own `x` breaks, so we set them every five years with `scale_x_continuous()` ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} # create labels from factor levels st_lbls <- paste0( levels(rugrats_babies_fct$year_range), collapse = ", ") labs_inst_rugrats_facet <- labs( title = "Rugrats baby names", caption = "Simulated data", subtitle = paste0("Time span: ", st_lbls), x = "Year", y = "Name") ggp2_inst_rugrats_facet <- ggplot(rugrats_babies_fct, mapping = aes(x = year, y = name)) + geom_point(aes(alpha = n, color = name), shape = "|", size = 3, show.legend = FALSE) + scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1980, 2005, by = 5)) + scale_alpha_continuous(range = c(0.35, 1)) + facet_wrap(year_range ~ group, scales = "free", ncol = 2) ggp2_inst_rugrats_facet + labs_inst_rugrats_facet ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](instance_chart_files/figure-html/code_graph_inst_facet-1.png){width=576} ::: ::: :::
